subject: Hypatia RFP: BYO-HSM onboarding steps, key transfer & TLS provisioning

Subject: Hypatia RFP: BYO-HSM onboarding steps, key transfer & TLS provisioning

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the rapid response to our RFP. A few of our security reviewers asked for a concise, operational playbook: specifically we need a step-by-step for BYO-HSM (HSM vendor agnostic but our preference is Thales/Luna), the allowed key import/export modes (wrapped import vs. remote attestation-only), and a clear statement on whether private key material ever leaves Hypatia's HSM in plaintext during onboarding.

We also need a TLS provisioning matrix: how Redwood manages server cert issuance for private endpoints (client certs vs. mTLS termination at load balancer), recommended cipher suites for our FIPS environment, and a timeline for cert rotation.

Can you provide an operational sequence, example commands or API calls, and the attestation evidence we should expect to receive? We're looking to finalize vendor selections by end of next week (10/29).

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Security
Hypatia Health

Subject: Re: Hypatia RFP: BYO-HSM onboarding steps, key transfer & TLS provisioning

Liam —

Appreciate the clear ask. I attached a concise operational playbook (hypatia_kms_playbook_v1.pdf) and a TLS provisioning matrix (hypatia_tls_provisioning_matrix.xlsx) that cover the items you listed. High-level answers up front:

- Private key material never leaves Hypatia's HSM in plaintext when using our recommended wrapped-import flow (customer wraps with a pre-shared import key or uses RSA/OAEP envelope).
- We support both wrapped import and remote attestation/telemetry-based trust; wrapped import is the only method that results in keys being resident in Redwood-managed HSMs in a customer-owned-wrapped form.
- For on-prem/private deployments (VPC/private plane) we can integrate with your HSM over PKCS#11 or KMIP; for hosted customers we support Bring-Your-Own-Key by registering attestation vouchers and allowing remote sealed key material transfers via an encrypted import session.

Attachments include: step-by-step sequences, example PKCS#11 import calls, recommended cipher suites (TLS1.2/TLS1.3 preferences), and sample attestation artifacts (quote format + expected fields).

Please review and tell us which flow you'd like us to expand into a runbook (wrapped-import into Redwood-managed key slots, or direct KMIP/PKCS#11 integration to Hypatia-provided HSMs).

Best,

Subject: Re: Hypatia RFP: BYO-HSM onboarding steps, key transfer & TLS provisioning

Thanks Dev — reviewed the attachments. A couple of clarifications from our engineering and compliance teams:

1) For wrapped-import: can Hypatia retain export protection so our HSM's wrapping key never leaves our control? We need to confirm that Redwood cannot unwrap keys without an HSM-protected key held by Hypatia.
2) For remote attestation: please enumerate the attestations you collect (quote, PCRs, firmware version, firmware attestation signatures) and whether Redwood will store the attestation artifacts long-term. Our retention policy requires attestation artifacts to be kept for 7 years.
3) TLS: we require mutual TLS for the private control-plane endpoints and prefer that cert rotation is automated with zero-downtime switchover. Do you have existing automation (ACME or internal CA integration) and timeline estimates for rotation across a 20-node dedicated cluster?

Could you loop in any internal contacts for lifecycle/ops and for evidence generation so we can confirm timelines?

Regards,
Priya
Priya Desai
Sr. Manager, Cloud Compliance
Hypatia Health

Subject: Re: Hypatia RFP: BYO-HSM onboarding steps, key transfer & TLS provisioning

Hi Priya / Liam —

Thanks for the great questions. I’m pulling lifecycle/ops and compliance evidence into this thread. Short answers here; see the attached playbook for exact commands and sample artifacts.

1) Wrapped-import key custody
- Hypatia retains sole control over the wrapping key. Our recommended wrapped-import pattern uses an import-wrapping public key provided by Hypatia. Redwood accepts only the wrapped blob; we never have access to the unwrapped key unless Hypatia explicitly performs an unwrap operation inside its HSM and re-exports unprotected material (which we do not recommend or support). We can provide a JSON snippet in the playbook that demonstrates "import-blob" fields and the expected PKCS#11 session parameters.

2) Attestation artifacts and retention
- We collect the following during an attestation flow: enclave/server quote, PCR values used for measurement, HSM firmware version string, attestation signature, and attestation certificate chain.
- Redwood can store attestation artifacts and link them to Hypatia's tenant ID. We will agree on a retention SLA; standard is 2 years but we can extend to 7 years under contract (we will surface associated storage costs). Evidence export: we provide a signed bundle (JSON + attachments) with timestamps and an integrity hash for each artifact.

3) TLS / rotation automation
- We support ACME integration for private/internal CAs when customers provide a reachable authority. For enterprise/private clusters we also support integration with internal CA tooling (HashiCorp Vault CA, Venafi).
- For mutual TLS we recommend terminating mTLS at the service mesh edge (Envoy sidecar) or at the dedicated load balancer depending on topology. Rotation timeline estimate for a 20-node cluster: automated orchestration completes in ~12–18 minutes for rolling cert swap (zero-downtime) provided health checks are green. We’ll provide a sample Helm job and CI hook to trigger rotation.

Next steps:
- If you want wrapped-import, confirm the wrapping key metadata (algorithm, key size, allowed usage) and we'll deliver a dry-run import session and example PKCS#11 commands.
- If you want Redwood to retain attestation artifacts for 7 years, we’ll include a line item in the SOW for extended evidence retention.

Looping in Rishi (platform ops) and Kimberly (compliance) to provide the dry-run schedule and evidence bundle format.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Hi Priya / Liam —

Following up with concrete next steps and a proposed dry-run schedule. Per Marissa's answers above, we confirm the engineering flow for wrapped-import and attestation:

Planned dry-run (target week of 10/26):
- Day 0 (prep): Hypatia provides wrapping public key (PEM) and key metadata (alg: RSA-OAEP-3072 or AES-GCM wrap), list of PKCS#11 labels expected, and the destination slot mapping.
- Day 1 (dry-run import): Redwood creates a dedicated import session; Hypatia produces a wrapped blob and an import manifest. Redwood validates the blob integrity, verifies the attestation bundle, and performs a non-destructive import into a locked key slot. No plaintext key material is exchanged.
- Day 2 (evidence & verification): Redwood exports an attestation bundle (signed JSON) and sample logs showing successful import and hash verification. Hypatia performs an end-to-end test by invoking a signing operation and verifying key responses.

Evidence artifacts we will provide after dry-run: import_manifest.json, attestation_bundle.tar.gz (quote, PCRs, firmware_version.txt, cert_chain.pem), import_session.log. We will sign bundles with our internal artifact-signing key and include SHA-256 digests.

Retention & SOW:
- We can retain attestation artifacts for 7 years under an addendum. I'll have Procurement and Finance prepare a cost estimate for archival storage (S3 Glacier tier with managed retention).

TLS automation:
- For mutual TLS automation we will provide an ACME-based controller (cert-manager) blueprint and a sample rotation job. For a 20-node cluster we'll run a rolling update via PodDisruptionBudget and readiness probes; average observed duration is 12–20 minutes depending on probe latency.

Please confirm:
- Preferred wrap algorithm (RSA-OAEP-3072 or AES-GCM)
- Whether you want Redwood to host keys post-import (Redwood-managed key usage) or solely act as a pass-through to your on-prem HSM (KMIP/PKCS#11 proxied).

If you confirm today we can schedule the dry-run for Mon 10/26 09:00 PT.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Platform Engineer — Key Management
Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
